scope: offline reduced CT appendix, two spherical proxy tools, material sensitivity; no force calibration or Isaac integration

matched_protocol.health_sampling: each 60 Hz control frame; internal solver-substep health is not recorded
matched_protocol.tool_geometry: two kinematic 3 mm radius spheres; not CAD jaws or wristed instruments
matched_protocol.tool_initialization: tools staged 50 mm above the tissue for 1 s gravity settling; then closest points on the settled tetrahedral boundary are used to place each sphere with a computed 5 mm surface clearance after radius
matched_protocol.approach: 9 mm over 1 s along the local surface normal, 0.5 s hold and 1 s retreat
matched_protocol.matched_control: same settled anatomy and tool trajectory, particle-tool contact disabled

material_input.interpretation: small-strain isotropic equivalent of ex-vivo 1 Hz, 1% shear storage modulus; not measured Young modulus or calibrated nonlinear material

historical_initialization_failure.reassessment: The tools were already colliding before commanded approach. Preserve this negative run, but do not interpret it as evidence that the literature-scaled material fails during a controlled grasp.

corrected_protocol_results.pair_status: passed numerical mesh-health criterion in this one matched run

force_measurement.reason: This coupon records geometry, contact point counts, and deformation only. It does not measure a calibrated tissue wrench or link it to instrument actuator force/torque.

interpretation: Safe, surface-distance-checked initialization eliminated early sphere overlap; all three contact-enabled runs had zero inverted tetrahedra at sampled control frames in this single trial per material.
Control also passed its matched unloaded run. Purulent and gangrenous unloaded runs failed, so those material conditions are not robustly validated despite their contact-enabled runs passing.
Simultaneous contact of both proxy spheres occurred, but this is not trocar-constrained bimanual instrument contact and does not establish a surgical grasp.

The initial overlaps explain the earlier apparent contact instability; the 960/1920 Hz and 32/64 iteration comparisons made before the start-pose correction are initialization-confounded. Their raw failure reports remain available locally.
privacy: Only source hashes, material values, aggregate contact counts, and element IDs are tracked. Mesh points, frames and solver arrays remain local and git-ignored.
remaining_limitations: One mesh and one trial per corrected material condition; repeatability and mesh/time-step convergence are not established
No calibrated force-displacement reference, rate response, compression stiffening, tissue tearing, or viscoelasticity
Spherical tools are not instrument CAD, articulated wrists, or trocar constrained arms
Two-way contact force transfer to the robot and Isaac runtime behavior are not verified
The 60 Hz health sampling can miss transient inversion inside solver substeps
